tagline: River roads circle a freight canal turned parkland in central New Jersey
intro: River Road winds beside the Millstone River; Canal Road follows the Delaware and Raritan Canal on the valley’s eastern side. Together they form the Millstone Valley Scenic Byway loop through central New Jersey. Its sponsor, the Millstone Valley Preservation Coalition, credits national and state designation to the valley’s scenery, historical importance and environmental integrity. State designation came in 2001, followed by national recognition in 2009. The drive occupies the river’s long, narrow floodplain, and its roads pass through eleven historic districts listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The roads draw on an older network of trails that followed and crossed the river in the homeland of the Lenni Lenape. Those trails became the area’s roads, including Canal Road and River Road. In 1777, the Continental Army marched up this valley after its victory at Princeton. The canal later carried coal, farm products and manufactured goods toward New York for a century. Land between the two roads now belongs to Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park.

Starting at Rocky Hill, the loop reaches Kingston before following the canal side north through Griggstown. At Griggstown, an original bridgetender’s house serves as the byway visitor center. Continue toward Millstone and East Millstone, linked near the loop’s northern end by County Route 514, then return along the river side.

moments.title: Rocky Hill
moments.text: Rocky Hill’s old nickname, the Devil’s Featherbed, described ground that was difficult to cross by horse and wagon before road improvements. In 1783, George Washington stayed at Rockingham, the Berrien family’s house. The village’s major growth came later, in the second quarter of the nineteenth century, as a stop between Princeton and New Brunswick. Its historic district includes the Dutch Reformed Church, built in 1856 in the Carpenter Gothic style. The district’s National Register listing recognizes its archaeology, architecture and commerce. Rockingham itself has been relocated; the byway listing places it in Kingston.

moments.title: Griggstown
moments.text: At Griggstown, the byway visitor center occupies an original canal bridgetender’s house. Inside, the kitchen is furnished to represent 1840–1860; the garden combines period medicinal plants with vegetables for the table. The settlement’s name reaches further back than the canal, to Benjamin Griggs and his gristmill on the Millstone River. That mill became a meeting place for European farmers and the center of the emerging community. The river and canal both pass through the village. The historic district also includes a bridgetender’s station and a locktender’s house, both built for the canal.
moments.notice: The visitor-center garden includes medicinal plants and table vegetables selected to represent the canal era.

moments.title: Millstone
moments.text: Millstone was once Somerset Courthouse, the county seat from 1738 until British forces burned it in 1779. After the Battle of Princeton in January 1777, Washington spent a night at the Van Doren house while his army camped nearby. They marched on to Pluckemin the next day, bound for winter quarters at Morristown. Another brief connection came with the Mercer and Somerset Railway in the 1870s: a bridge linked it across the river to the Pennsylvania Railroad’s line. The arrangement ended before the 1880s, but remnants of the bridge remain visible.
